newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends up slightly against dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends up slightly against dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up slightly on Tuesday at 8.2932, from Monday's 8.2935 against the U.S. dollar on Shanghai's foreign exchange interbank market despite intervention from the central bank, traders said.
The People's Bank of China intervened a few minutes before closing to prevent the yuan from rising sharply, they said.

The yuan opened slightly up at 8.2933 and remained stable around 8.2930 early in the session, touching an intraday low of 8.2935. It then rose steadily and hit a high of 8.2909 in late trading before the central bank's intervention, traders said.
Trading was more active than on Monday with most transactions done at 8.2928, traders said.
One dealer said the intervention depressed the yuan's uptrend and weakened strong pro-yuan sentiment.
"The intervention reminds us of a similar move at the same time last year when the central bank made use of thin trading during the holiday to force the yuan down," he said.
The market is largely dominated by a holiday mood, with the lunar new year holiday beginning on February 7, traders said.
A second dealer said that if the central bank continued to invervene in the market, the yuan's upward trend of the past few months could come to an end.
He said he expected the yuan to move around the 8.2930 level on Wednesday.
The yuan closed up at 6.8000 from 6.8270 against 100 Japanese yen and up slightly at an intraday high of 1.0688 from 1.0693 against the Hong Kong dollar.
